# Architecture and decisions

## Ownership

- **ARC-001** [review] Area: Web and Windows/macOS presentation; Source of truth: `apps/web/src`; Tauri host/adapters in `apps/desktop`
- **ARC-002** [review] Area: Native presentation; Source of truth: `apps/mobile/src`; Expo, native controls, no DOM imports
- **ARC-003** [review] Area: Independently deployable API; Source of truth: `apps/api/src`; NestJS, PostgreSQL, module-owned services
- **ARC-004** [review] Area: Runtime contracts and settings; Source of truth: `packages/contracts/src`; strict schemas at trust boundaries
- **ARC-005** [review] Area: Client models, transport and navigation; Source of truth: `packages/api-client/src`; injected platform adapters
- **ARC-006** [review] Area: Portable business rules; Source of truth: `packages/domain/src`; no app/UI/server/native imports
- **ARC-007** [review] Area: Design tokens; Source of truth: `packages/design-tokens/tokens.css`; generated native exports
- **ARC-008** [review] Area: Workspace scripts/dependencies; Source of truth: Root and workspace `package.json`, root npm lockfile
- **ARC-009** [review] Controllers validate requests; application services authorize and orchestrate transactions; domain rules own invariants; repositories/adapters own persistence/external calls. Shared packages never import applications. Keep native integrations outside browser code. Do not introduce another state, settings, styling or component framework without a demonstrated need.

## Finding every screen

- **ARC-010** [review] Use `packages/api-client/src/workspace-navigation.ts`, `apps/web/src/app/router.tsx`, and the registries inspected by `scripts/check-parity.mjs`. Run `npm run check:parity` for shared/web/native coverage. Public storefront is web-only; its management screens require native parity. The component showcase is `/#/design-system`; it operates on local examples, not business records.
- **ARC-011** [review] Implemented areas include organization/access management, catalog/pricing, inventory ledger/counts/storage/transfers, purchasing/suppliers, customers/credit, POS/shifts/receipts/returns, staff/expenses, reporting, notifications/approvals/audit, settings, trading/accounting foundations, bounded offline cash and storefront publication management. Inspect the owning module and tests before calling a sub-feature complete. A route existing is not proof that every workflow works.

## Accepted decisions

- **ARC-012** [review] These rules preserve prior decisions; future behavior is not implicitly implemented by documenting it.
- **ARC-013** [review] Accepted product/domain decisions are owned by [security and data](security-and-data.md#accepted-product-decisions); preserve them during redesign.
- **ARC-014** [review] Publication management is implemented; guest checkout/fulfillment is not established by that implementation. Store-scoped `onlineStore.view` supports authorized read; business-wide `onlineStore.manage` controls writes. Manager read supersedes older “owners only” documentation. Readiness and availability revalidate on server; hints only invalidate clients. Media previews require authenticated scope, trusted hosts, public-address pinning, no redirects/credential forwarding, byte/time/rate caps and post-fetch authorization.
- **ARC-015** [review] Rejected designs remain rejected: client-only authorization; exposing internal APIs publicly; new PO sent state; fake stock reservations; blind last-write-wins; deleting financial evidence; payment inferred from delivery; persistent analytics; duplicate pricing systems.

## Platform and product limits

- **ARC-016** [review] Web, Windows and macOS are release gates. Mobile code parity remains required but is not a launch gate. Tauri reuses web UI; neither browser tests nor a macOS build qualify installed Windows/WebView behavior. Expo exports prove bundling, not device storage/printing/deep links.
- **ARC-017** [review] Full statutory accounting, historical inventory valuation/COGS, 3D, automatic updates, MFA and external payment/provider delivery must not be advertised unless subsequently implemented and qualified. AI is disabled-provider, permission-checked navigation scaffolding; no secret-bearing prompts or autonomous business execution.
- **ARC-018** [review] Historical feature specifications, decision context/rejected options, milestone prompts and evidence are preserved in the consolidation archive described in [development](development.md#documentation-history). Consult them for a specifically requested historical item; do not execute old milestones by default.

# Security, data and offline rules

## Identity and authorization

- **SEC-001** [review] Invitation onboarding; operator-issued password recovery. Keep established password hashing, session expiry/renewal, rate limits and revocation. Never invent a successful email/SMS verification.
- **SEC-002** [review] Browser credentials use HttpOnly cookies with production Secure/SameSite and origin/CSRF checks. Mobile uses SecureStore; desktop credentials remain ephemeral in memory. Client environment variables are public.
- **SEC-003** [review] Every protected read/write, export, job, socket and retry resolves authenticated membership, tenant, permission and store/warehouse/resource scope. Client IDs, hidden controls and notification delivery grant no authority.
- **SEC-004** [review] Hide inaccessible routes/actions in UI; keep backend checks. Account/business changes, expiry, denial and explicit lock clear sensitive in-memory state. Browser tab hiding/focus is not a session lock: revalidate in the background without remounting an unexpired workspace; enforce expiry on return even if timers were suspended. Native background session locking remains unchanged. Do not reset user preferences to work around a session failure.
- **SEC-005** [review] Use scoped foreign keys/unique constraints, bounded queries and safe validation. Cross-business trade authorizes each party separately. RLS is not a substitute for existing application checks and must not be claimed universally active.
- **SEC-006** [review] Mutations commit source/projection/audit/idempotency/change records atomically where locally transactional. Authorize before replaying an idempotency receipt; reject a reused key with a different payload.
- **SEC-007** [review] Generic transports never automatically retry mutations. Protected retries retain their original ID and payload. An unknown response is not proof of failure; inspect/reconcile before creating a new operation.
- **SEC-008** [review] Log actor, scope, operation, reason and safe diagnostic context. Never log passwords, cookies, tokens, keys, payment secrets or unnecessary PII. Show actionable safe errors; keep technical correlation IDs secondary.
- **SEC-009** [review] Production uses validated config, verified database TLS, HTTPS, narrow CORS/CSP, bounded requests and durable abuse limits. CORS is not authorization. Seeds/mocks stay explicitly development/test-only.

## Stock and money

- **SEC-010** [review] LedgerCore owns immutable inventory movements and transactional balance projections. Preserve actor/time/source/reason, base-unit precision and movement references; never overwrite stock silently.
- **SEC-011** [review] Reservations, damaged stock, in-transit stock and physical on hand are distinct. Lock affected stock keys consistently; test concurrent allocation, partial transfers/receipts, counts and rollback.
- **SEC-012** [review] Counts reconcile against observations/revision and intervening movements. Transfers require both endpoints. Inter-business trade status does not post either party's stock/cash.
- **SEC-013** [review] Quantities use exact six-place decimal rules; money uses currency minor units. Preserve currency exponent, original units, rounding/tax/discount order. Never sum currencies or use binary floating-point financial totals.
- **SEC-014** [review] Prices/taxes/discounts on posted sales are immutable snapshots. Current product edits affect new quotes; checkout revalidates server-side. Display-currency preference is not FX conversion.
- **SEC-015** [review] AR/AP derive from obligations, credits and allocations. Prevent overpayment, over-return, over-refund and negative till cash transactionally. Return credits apply original cumulative rounding and reduce unpaid credit before cash refunds.
- **SEC-016** [review] Goods return, credit, refund and replacement sale are separate linked facts. Damaged returns do not increase sellable stock; non-restockable returns do not increase stock. Closed shifts and posted journals are immutable.
- **SEC-017** [review] Accounting is limited balanced source posting, not statutory accounting/valuation. Source uniqueness is separate from request identity. Reversing a journal does not reverse its sale/stock/payment.

## Posting boundaries

- **SEC-018** [review] Confirmed event: Online order acceptance (future); Stock: Reserve real sellable quantity only; Money / journal intent: No sale revenue or cash; backordered remainder unallocated
- **SEC-019** [review] Confirmed event: Cancel unfulfilled remainder; Stock: Release hold once; Money / journal intent: Refund any advance separately; no fictitious stock increase
- **SEC-020** [review] Confirmed event: Physical dispatch/pickup; Stock: Deduct fulfilled goods and consume hold once; Money / journal intent: Recognize fulfilled sale/AR; debit settlement/AR, credit net revenue/tax
- **SEC-021** [review] Confirmed event: Cash physically collected; Stock: None; Money / journal intent: Open-shift cash receipt; debit cash, credit AR or customer advance
- **SEC-022** [review] Confirmed event: Confirmed courier/bank collection; Stock: None; Money / journal intent: Debit relevant clearing, credit AR/advance; no till cash
- **SEC-023** [review] Confirmed event: Advance applied at fulfillment; Stock: No extra deduction; Money / journal intent: Debit advance, credit AR; no duplicate revenue
- **SEC-024** [review] Confirmed event: Clearing remitted to bank/till; Stock: None; Money / journal intent: Debit bank/cash, credit clearing; no second customer payment/revenue
- **SEC-025** [review] Confirmed event: Order complete; Stock: None beyond fulfillment; Money / journal intent: No extra posting
- **SEC-026** [review] Confirmed event: Authorized return received; Stock: Disposition-specific movement once; Money / journal intent: Linked credit: reverse revenue/tax into settlement/AR
- **SEC-027** [review] Confirmed event: Approved refund actually paid; Stock: None merely from payment; Money / journal intent: Debit settlement/advance, credit actual cash/bank/clearing
- **SEC-028** [review] Confirmed event: POS checkout; Stock: Existing immediate handover movement; Money / journal intent: Existing sale/payment sources, once each
- **SEC-029** [review] Confirmed event: Offline captured sale; Stock: Provisional local evidence; Money / journal intent: No confirmed server posting until authorized successful sync
- **SEC-030** [review] Partial events cover only confirmed portions. Future online source posting must persist a durable intent with source/audit effects; pending journals are not posted journals. These posting rules preserve design decisions, not a claim that guest fulfillment or clearing is implemented.

## Offline contract

- **SEC-031** [review] Only prepared, encrypted, bounded **cash sales**, carts and catalog/price snapshots may operate offline. Credit, refunds, approvals, purchasing, counts, transfers and online-store administration require online authority.
- **SEC-032** [review] Policy defaults off; grants bind account/business/device/warehouse/currency/shift/access fingerprint/policy/immutable price snapshot. Preserve configured 5–480 minute lease, cash/quantity/discount limits and changed-price policy.
- **SEC-033** [review] Current preparation is bounded to 250 active variants, one currency and warehouse-root stock. Cached stock is an allowance, never a global reservation; server shortages stay conflicts.
- **SEC-034** [review] Vault is an authenticated encrypted document: AES-256-GCM, random 96-bit nonce, independent salt and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 (600,000 iterations). No account password, session token or plaintext customer profiles. Separate passphrase loss has no recovery backdoor.
- **SEC-035** [review] Web uses IndexedDB; Tauri and native use transactional SQLite WAL adapters. Origin/account/device partitions, compare-and-swap writes, atomic cart/outbox and projection/cursor commits remain mandatory.
- **SEC-036** [review] Lock/background clears in-memory keys. Expiry blocks new sales without deleting pending evidence. Detect backward-clock movement; hostile device clocks remain a known limitation. Revocation discovery is bounded by the original lease, not instantaneous offline.
- **SEC-037** [review] Upload reauthorizes current scope/policy/shift/stock and operation time; normal grace is 24 hours for in-grant sales. Older/revoked/conflicting records require authorized reconciliation, not deletion or recreated sales.
- **SEC-038** [review] Batches max 20, durable atomic claims before I/O, stable IDs/hashes, exponential jitter backoff capped five minutes, eight failures require review. Late replies never downgrade confirmed results.
- **SEC-039** [review] Schema migration/backup/restore must preserve pending work; unknown/tampered versions fail closed. Backup encrypted envelopes and consistent SQLite WAL state. Never advise clearing storage with unsynced sales; outbox retention cap is 1,000 records.
- **SEC-040** [review] Readiness recovery triggers eligible sync; polling/backoff recovers missed events. Progress counts server confirmations, not bytes/network availability. Pending/sending/synced/rejected/conflict remain distinct with reviewable receipts.
- **SEC-041** [review] Offline shell service worker caches public app assets only, never private API/auth/analytics. Development Vite and Expo web export are not proof of offline browser restart. Do not force updates mid-checkout.
- **SEC-042** [review] Revision polling/WebSocket tickets are scoped invalidation hints, never command channels or confirmation. Reconnect rereads authoritative data; delta cursors bind scope/currency and commit with cache updates.

## Public and analytics boundaries

- **SEC-043** [review] Published reads expose allowlisted fields only, never costs/suppliers/private inventory/customer data. Guest writes/event ingestion require distinct implementation, narrow guards, stable identities and abuse limits. Status tokens must be random, digest-stored, bounded, revocable and scoped to minimal status; redact URL/log/referrer exposure. Staff authority cannot be inherited by a guest endpoint.
- **SEC-044** [review] Analytics may retain an authorized, timestamped **in-memory** view during transient failure only until session expiry/lock. Partition by account/business/permissions/query/currency/timezone; clear on denial, switch, logout, explicit lock, native background or restart. Browser tab hiding may retain this bounded in-memory view until session expiry; it does not authorize offline analytics or persist data. No analytics in SQLite, IndexedDB, vaults, backups or service worker. Intended net reporting counts return credits once, not both credit and refund, with business-timezone/DST boundaries and separate currencies.
- **SEC-045** [review] Notification inbox removal sets `business_deliveries.dismissed_at`; audit events and delivery evidence remain. Read/unread/removal revalidate recipient, tenant, permission and location scope. Actor emails in notifications and audit history require `users.read`. Member removal archives only that business membership; customer archival retains transactions and rejects outstanding exposure. Never present either operation as global account or ledger deletion.
- **SEC-046** [review] Rich product/online descriptions keep the existing string field: legacy values are plain text; `<!--inventory-description:v1-->` marks allowlisted HTML. Contracts normalize marked writes; `descriptionText` drives readiness, and renderers consume parsed nodes. Only paragraphs, emphasis, lists and HTTP(S)/mailto links survive; scripts, embeds, arbitrary attributes and unsafe links do not. Do not render this field as unrestricted HTML. The existing 2,000-character serialized limit applies; no migration or legacy rewrite is needed.
- **SEC-047** [review] Quill 2.0.3 has an open HTML-export advisory ([GHSA-v3m3-f69x-jf25](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-v3m3-f69x-jf25)). Its export is untrusted: sanitize it before persistence and render parsed allowlisted nodes, never exported HTML directly. Keep those protections and review upstream fixes; dependency audit is not clean.

## Accepted product decisions

- **SEC-048** [review] Decision: PO sending; Rule / consequence: Keep `ordered`; optional sent time/method, UI “Ordered / Sent”; no new state or stock/cash effect.
- **SEC-049** [review] Decision: Prices; Rule / consequence: No named price lists. Storefront uses the existing default-store resolver and explicit online overrides; never create a parallel calculator or change POS price through an online override.
- **SEC-050** [review] Decision: Adjustment reasons; Rule / consequence: Built-in codes plus optional tenant custom codes; preserve historical reason snapshots and existing free text.
- **SEC-051** [review] Decision: Refund approvals; Rule / consequence: Cumulative per-sale, per-currency thresholds through the approval queue; absent policy requires approval. No self-approval or split-request bypass. Execution revalidates independently. Do not assume every refund path implements this yet.
- **SEC-052** [review] Decision: Undo; Rule / consequence: Authorized, idempotent linked compensation; never erase committed stock, money or audit history.
- **SEC-053** [review] Decision: Public API; Rule / consequence: Separate published-only projection, not internal catalog controllers. Narrow guest commands and event ingestion require separate guards and abuse budgets before implementation.
- **SEC-054** [review] Decision: Sellable stock; Rule / consequence: On hand − reserved − damaged − buffer, per SKU and allocation pool; buffer once, transit separate. Backorders are identified unallocated demand, not fictional holds.
- **SEC-055** [review] Decision: Readiness; Rule / consequence: Content/price failures auto-delist; zero availability remains active as Sold out or hidden by policy. Stock is not a content blocker.
- **SEC-056** [review] Decision: Payments; Rule / consequence: Pickup/COD/manual transfer design only; COD unpaid until confirmed collection, transfer uses clearing. Card providers disabled. Configuration does not imply guest checkout exists.
- **SEC-057** [review] Decision: Posting; Rule / consequence: Order, payment, fulfillment and journal events are distinct; see [integrity](security-and-data.md#posting-boundaries).
- **SEC-058** [review] Decision: Analytics; Rule / consequence: Online-only, in-memory cached/as-of views. Intended shared POS/online aggregation uses business timezone and net returns; do not describe legacy UTC/gross queries as migrated without tests.

# Design system

## Start here

- **DS-001** [review] Reuse the actual components at `/#/design-system` before writing UI. Web and Tauri use the existing shadcn-style/Radix primitives and Vaul drawers with small token-based adjustments; do not install another component library. Native uses React Native equivalents, never DOM wrappers. A feature owns its state/permissions; primitives own presentation and accessibility.
- **DS-002** [review] Responsibility: Primitive controls; Web (relative to `apps/web/src`): `components/ui/`; Native (relative to `apps/mobile/src`): `ui/Controls.tsx`, `ui/Themed.tsx`, `ui/SelectChoice.tsx`
- **DS-003** [review] Responsibility: Reusable application patterns; Web (relative to `apps/web/src`): `components/common/`; Native (relative to `apps/mobile/src`): `ui/`
- **DS-004** [review] Responsibility: Shell/navigation; Web (relative to `apps/web/src`): `components/layout/` and app routing; Native (relative to `apps/mobile/src`): `shell/` and navigation registries
- **DS-005** [review] Responsibility: Business UI; Web (relative to `apps/web/src`): `features/<feature>/`; Native (relative to `apps/mobile/src`): `<feature>/`
- **DS-006** [review] Responsibility: Appearance adapter; Web (relative to `apps/web/src`): `theme/Appearance.tsx`, `theme/preferences.css`; Native (relative to `apps/mobile/src`): `theme.tsx`

## Tokens and user preferences

- **DS-007** [review] `packages/design-tokens/tokens.css` is the palette/metric source. Run `npm run build:shared` to generate native exports. Use semantic surface/text/primary/border/focus/status/navigation/table/chart tokens; use spacing, typography, radius and elevation tokens instead of feature-local values. Physical print/barcode black and white are deliberate exceptions. Layout breakpoints, aspect ratios and actual media dimensions may be explicit; do not replace them blindly.
- **DS-008** [review] `packages/contracts/src/settings.ts` owns schema/defaults and `resolveSettings`. Approved redesign migration: cosmetic fields resolve platform defaults → explicit account values → device constraints; business defaults/enforced and platform enforced cosmetics are retained in policy records but no longer applied. Currency and pagination retain existing policy precedence. Security/offline/operational policy is unchanged; no second settings store.
- **DS-009** [review] Preference: Appearance; Required behavior: Light, dark, system; system reacts to OS changes, including portals
- **DS-010** [review] Accent identities remain blue/teal/violet/rose/amber; apply to links, focus and charts only. Primary controls and selected/sidebar surfaces are neutral in both themes.
- **DS-011** [review] Bundle Geist/GeistMono, Karla/Lora and license notices. New selections offer bundled assets; an existing system/serif/monospace/local choice remains available with its prior fallback. Never download a font at runtime.
- **DS-012** [review] Preference: Text size; Required behavior: Small/medium/large scale headings, controls, menus, tables and help; native OS scaling remains enabled
- **DS-013** [review] Preference: Radius; Required behavior: Rounded: restrained corners; circle: pill controls/avatars and larger card corners; multiline fields stay readable
- **DS-014** [review] Density compact/default/comfortable changes contextual gaps, rows and toolbar minima, independently of controlSize small/medium/large. Text and icon choices remain independent; controls grow for text and preserve coarse-web 44px/native 48px touch targets.
- **DS-015** [review] Preference: Icon size; Required behavior: Existing small/medium/large metrics; named icons, consistent stroke and accessible icon-only labels
- **DS-016** [review] Animation off/minimal/full changes feedback only; OS reduced motion always wins. Legacy disabled/reduced retains no nonessential motion until explicit new selection. Minimal uses opacity/shadow transitions; preserve static pending feedback.
- **DS-017** [review] Preference: Effects; Required behavior: Optional decorative elevations; disabling never removes focus, selection or functional feedback
- **DS-018** [review] Charts numbers/balanced/charts changes prominence, never calculations or access to exact values/records/exports. ChartPresentation provides numeric values plus a chart reveal in numbers mode; retain legacy visualization choices until explicit selection.
- **DS-019** [review] Preference: States; Required behavior: Simple/enhanced presentation, same data/error semantics; enhanced empty states have icon/title/description and only permitted relevant actions
- **DS-020** [review] Preference: Pagination; Required behavior: Existing pages/scroll behavior; no paginator for one page, keep bounded data loading and stable selection
- **DS-021** [review] Preference: Currency; Required behavior: Existing supported codes/symbol formatter; no conversion or reinterpretation of posted monetary values
- **DS-022** [review] Settings controls belong in Preferences, not repeated on every feature page. Keep user choice effective throughout mounted screens and overlays without resetting drafts. Explain enforced choices rather than offering an ineffective toggle.

## Screen contract

- **DS-023** [review] One authoritative heading/description and consistent action placement; preserve existing route shell and history-aware back action. Auth has its own layout; no business controls stacked under login.
- **DS-024** [review] One wrapping collection toolbar: search with leading icon/clear, filter badge/summary, view tabs where supported, relevant refresh and permission-gated creation/export. Debounce/cancel reads; never retry unsafe commands generically.
- **DS-025** [review] Existing Table/TableScroll: aligned headers/cells, fixed narrow selection column, select-all in header, right-aligned actions, tabular numeric values, token zebra rows. Wide tables scroll inside a named region, not the whole page.
- **DS-026** [review] Use StatusBadge with explicit semantic tone, never an unstyled `status-badge` span. Status is text plus color. Links underline on hover; icon actions use real tooltips and keyboard names.
- **DS-027** [review] Cards reflow with content-driven columns; preserve names, units and prices. Show selection only with authorized bulk actions. Selected counts appear only when relevant.
- **DS-028** [review] Keep cart below the sticky header with internal scrolling and visible checkout; present authoritative totals and unknown/failed states honestly.
- **DS-029** [review] Stores/terminals open read-only details first; scoped writers get Edit, Activate/Deactivate and confirmed Archive. Archival preserves history, is permanent and is not hard deletion; the server enforces parent/dependent-record rules.
- **DS-030** [review] Drawers use existing FormSheet/SidePanel and focus/keyboard/safe-area handling. Keep small confirmations in ConfirmDialog. Do not replace platform-accessible selection/menu behavior with hand-built clickable divs.
- **DS-031** [review] Empty search explains no matches; empty collections offer permitted creation; failures offer a real retry; offline/sync UI distinguishes local persistence from remote confirmation.
- **DS-032** [review] Support 320px through desktop widths, large text, keyboard, visible focus, meaningful labels/errors, screen readers, reduced motion and touch. No feature removal to fit a smaller viewport.

## Web component API reference

- **DS-033** [review] Use TypeScript declarations in the linked implementation as the exact required/optional/default prop contract; the existing showcase exercises real components. Shared additions require inline prop documentation, a local-state showcase example, meaningful interaction tests and an update here. Avoid a second prose copy of every prop signature that will become stale.
- **DS-034** [review] Component source: `components/common/Layout.tsx`; Use / limitation: Page main landmark/skip link; Stack/Cluster/Grid/Panel layout. One main per route, avoid unnecessary card nesting.
- **DS-035** [review] Component source: `components/common/FormField.tsx`; Use / limitation: Label, hint and error associations; spread supplied control props onto actual input. ErrorSummary focuses invalid controls.
- **DS-036** [review] Component source: `components/ui/FormControls.tsx`; Use / limitation: Shared Input/Textarea/Select; use native validation and existing schemas. Search only for sufficiently large/dynamic option sets.
- **DS-037** [review] Component source: `components/common/IconButton.tsx`; Use / limitation: Named icon + label/tooltip; never encode permission or command behavior in the primitive.
- **DS-038** [review] Component source: `components/ui/StatusBadge.tsx`; Use / limitation: `children`; optional `tone`: neutral (default), success, warning, error, info. Not an action.
- **DS-039** [review] Component source: `components/common/SearchControl.tsx`; Use / limitation: Controlled text/suggestions, clear and keyboard listbox; owner supplies bounded, cancellable reads.
- **DS-040** [review] Component source: `components/common/FilterButton.tsx`, `ViewTabs.tsx`, `OverflowTabs.tsx`; Use / limitation: Active filter summary, list/grid and overflow chevrons. OverflowTabs child uses the established settings-tabs style.
- **DS-041** [review] Component source: `components/ui/Table.tsx`; Use / limitation: Semantic table and named keyboard-scroll region; caller owns sort/filter/page/selection.
- **DS-042** [review] Component source: `components/common/FormSheet.tsx`, `ConfirmDialog.tsx`; Use / limitation: Controlled drawer or confirmation with title/description/focus. Preserve pending/dismissal rules; model owns async work.
- **DS-043** [review] Component source: `components/common/AsyncState.tsx`; Use / limitation: Loading/empty/error; preserve announcements and safe retry identity.
- **DS-044** [review] Component source: `components/common/MetricCard.tsx`; Use / limitation: Label/value/unit, optional primary treatment; no fabricated trend or calculation.
- **DS-045** [review] Component source: `components/ui/Accordion.tsx`, `Popover.tsx`, `Tooltip.tsx`; Use / limitation: Existing keyboard/portal primitives; no hover-only critical information or clipped actions.

## Native component API reference

- **DS-046** [review] Native `ui/Themed.tsx` Text/TextInput resolve font, size, colors and state; `ui/Controls.tsx` provides Action/Field/Choice. `ui/IconAction.tsx` takes an accessible label and native icon name. Use `ui/StatusBadge.tsx`, `MetricCard.tsx`, `Surface.tsx`, `SearchControl.tsx`, `FilterButton.tsx` and `ViewTabs.tsx` for equivalent patterns. `ui/SidePanel.tsx` owns modal safe areas, scrolling and optional footer. Native controls support system text scaling; keep minimum touch targets even in compact mode. Local desktop font availability does not imply that font exists on a phone.
- **DS-047** [review] Browser/React Native Web tests do not qualify VoiceOver/TalkBack, native modals, keyboard avoidance or installed WebViews. Use the release checklist in [development](development.md#release-qualification).
- **DS-048** [review] Collection toolbars use `RecordCollection.toolbar` for search/filters and `.actions` for permission-aware creation commands after the view tabs (native equivalent: `ui/RecordCollection`). The navigation-control showcase demonstrates local-only search, list/grid and creation. Team contains employment/salary records; Expenses is separate. Customer retention lives in Business settings. Product edit drawers reuse ProductChannels for online actions and the versioned catalog command for activation; catalog inactivity also prevents POS sales and online publication.
- **DS-049** [review] POS quantity edits keep controls available during read-only repricing; checkout requires a fresh authoritative quote. Product discovery does not treat display currency as a listing filter. Parent activation never revives independently disabled SKUs; an older inactive default SKU may need activation in Variants and pricing.
- **DS-050** [review] Base desktop controls are 30/34/40px by controlSize, independently of 32/40/48px density row minima; page titles are 22px. Text scales, wrapping and touch minima may increase actual dimensions. Product cards use content-driven columns; hover actions remain reachable by focus/touch.
- **DS-051** [review] `components/common/ExportRecords.tsx` and native `ui/ExportRecords.tsx` accept required `headers`/`rows` (readonly string arrays), optional `name` and `label`; defaults are `records-shown` / “Export shown records”. Use only already-authorized visible rows; exports protect spreadsheet formula cells and preserve exact strings. RecordCollection includes a working showcase example. Exporting is not an all-pages/background report job. Drawer action groups use `drawer-actions` for two-column layout.
- **DS-052** [review] Security event lists use readable event/outcome labels and `MMM D, YYYY h:mm A` device-local time; details include weekday, seconds and zone. Drawers render labelled loaded event data, not JSON or another detail request. Actor labels use the authorized account email until personal names exist; identifiers remain secondary references.
- **DS-053** [review] Business notification drawers follow the same labelled-detail pattern using the business timezone, full event/read timestamps and secondary record references. Render the authorized loaded inbox record; preserve read/unread/dismiss commands and never invent missing actor names or transaction details.
- **DS-054** [review] Inventory is the combined product/stock workspace: Products & pricing reuses the catalog editor, variants, units, pricing and listing controls; Stock & movements reuses the ledger workflows. Show sections by their existing read permissions and retain command-level write/scope checks. `/catalog` is a hidden compatibility entry; navigation and product search use `/inventory`.
- **DS-055** [review] Product setup stays in one drawer: save Details, then Price & units, Quantity and optional Listing availability. The primary price form saves an immediate price; scheduled prices/variants/promotions remain advanced. Quantity records base-unit opening/add/remove movements at a selected warehouse root, never overwrites a balance. Each step saves independently, preserves confirmed earlier steps and enforces its original permissions.
- **DS-056** [review] POS uses scoped available stock to label tracked products with zero/negative stock “Sold” and disable card/detail/search additions; untracked or unknown availability is not sold out. Background catalog/pricing refreshes keep loaded content visible. A confirmed save followed by a failed refresh must say it was saved and offer a read-only reload, never imply that the mutation needs repeating.
- **DS-057** [review] Drawer widths are view-local, not account preferences. Shared `DrawerContent` uses `DrawerResizeHandle` (content ref + onResize callback) for edge dragging, 16px arrow-key steps, Home/End bounds and double-click reset; width stays within 320px and viewport minus 32px. Phone drawers fill the viewport, with no splitter. Native `SidePanel` uses `PanelResizeHandle` (width, maximum, onChange) for tablet edge dragging and screen-reader increment/decrement; small screens and menus retain their responsive layouts. These handles only change presentation, never form drafts or save/close behavior. The web NavigationControlsDemo and native showcase demonstrate the actual drawers; native gestures still require device qualification.
- **DS-058** [review] Product details: failed saves keep the draft and show a dismissible error toast (native: pinned panel notice); field errors stay beside accessible controls and reveal their section. `FormSection.open/onOpenChange` controls native sections to reveal validation errors; the native showcase demonstrates it. SKU checks debounce 350 ms and cancel stale reads; unavailable checks never claim uniqueness. The business-scoped server constraint remains authoritative, including concurrent saves.
- **DS-059** [review] SKU feedback uses an in-input check/X with accessible tooltips; the duplicate message has a hover/focus/tap product preview, limited by backend product-read permission. Native `Field.trailing` and `errorAccessory` keep equivalent affordances within the control and beside its error (showcase examples included).
- **DS-060** [review] Overview Sales trend has no collapsible daily-figures footer. The selected overview period controls its server snapshot, dates, totals and points; exact values remain available through the accessible web table/native bar labels.
- **DS-061** [review] Warehouse & storage (`/storage`) opens the searchable Locations list first, with Browse hierarchy as the secondary view under one warehouse selector on web/desktop and native mobile. Search, view controls, export and commands share the collection toolbar. Warehouse balances open on demand in a drawer; hierarchy stock uses a numeric table (labelled native cards). Location details and labels open read-only, with an authorized Edit location tab; creation and within-warehouse movement retain existing permissions and ledger commands. `/warehouse-view` remains a hidden compatibility route to this workspace. Facility administration and Stock counts & scanning remain separate workflows. Switching warehouse resets location navigation and pagination; switching tabs reloads the visible data.
- **DS-062** [review] Storage workspace tabs reuse the label-only Radix `view-tabs` treatment (native Settings tab treatment). The shell owns the page title; do not add a visible “Storage view” legend or duplicate introductory header.

## Rich descriptions and storage workspace

- **DS-063** [review] Product and online-description forms use `RichTextEditor` (web `components/common/`, native `ui/`) with controlled `value`/`onChange`; web also requires `id`/`label`, native requires `label`. Optional disabled/error associations preserve form validation. Use `RichDescription` with `value` for displays, never raw HTML. The showcase demonstrates both. Quill supports bold, italic, underline, lists and safe links; assets are local and generated for mobile by `build:shared`. Native uses an isolated WebView, Expo web an iframe; native font availability and keyboard/device behavior require qualification. Existing plain descriptions remain unchanged; the 2,000-character limit includes rich markup.
- **DS-064** [review] Storage uses one top row: Locations/Hierarchy tabs → Export locations/Create storage location/Move stock → warehouse selector. Actions retain their permissions and selected warehouse in either tab. Export covers loaded locations only. `RecordCollection.showExport` defaults to true; set false only when a parent supplies export (see showcase).

## Locked redesign direction and migration boundary

- **DS-065** [review] Use a light-default neutral enterprise foundation, restrained statuses and borders, neutral primary action fills, accent links/focus/charts and neutral selected surfaces. Use canonical tokens, never a second page palette.
- **DS-066** [review] Exactly five target axes: theme light/dark/system, density compact/default/comfortable, control size small/medium/large, animation off/minimal/full, charts numbers/balanced/charts. Keep accent, radius, font, text size, icon size, pagination, effects, states, currency and other existing choices without reinterpreting their saved values. No new border or typography setting; sidebar collapse remains per-device UI state.
- **DS-067** [review] Apply defaults only to missing raw fields: light theme, compact desktop/default native or coarse-pointer density, medium controls, minimal motion, balanced charts, Geist. Preserve explicit legacy choices; no default materialization on read. Account writes remain version checked and single attempt.
- **DS-068** [review] Approved cosmetic migration is read-time and non-destructive: preserve stored policy JSON and disclose retired cosmetic enforcement in settings. Account appearance is stable across business switches; enforced currency/pagination and security/operational constraints remain authoritative.
- **DS-069** [review] Geist assets are pinned by SHA and checksum in `packages/design-tokens/fonts/geist-source.json`; font license is distributed through the generated token package and both showcases. Deploy compatible settings server and clients together: older strict schemas may reject new preference keys.

- **DS-070** [enforced: npm run audit:ui] Design check rejects new static literal/control violations against the reviewed baseline and reports removed ones; it is not a visual/accessibility proof. Shared table/selection rules live in `theme/shared-collections.css`, shared control/command/collection rules in `theme/shared-controls.css`; feature layout remains in its owning sheet.
- **DS-071** [review] Local showcases expose density, control size, animation and chart choices without saving account records. Common chart presentation maps `components/common/ChartPresentation.tsx` to native `ui/ChartPresentation.tsx`; both accept label, chart children and exact values. Existing SearchControl/FilterButton/ViewTabs/RecordCollection/QuantityControl/MetricCard/AsyncState/WarehouseSelect/ExportRecords map to same-named native ui components; FormSheet maps to SidePanel, ConfirmDialog to ConfirmAction, FormField to Field, DataValue to DataRow, and Table/TableScroll to RecordTable. Native APIs adapt platform semantics, never import DOM primitives.
- **DS-072** [review] Verify default/corner combinations in both themes: all densities × control sizes, small/large text, both radius styles, all accents, reduced motion, retained fonts and account/business switching. Evidence in `.ai/reports/redesign/phase-3-validation` distinguishes CSS probes, actual control interactions and platform limitations; native-web tests do not qualify installed devices.

- **DS-073** [review] Shell collapse/width are optional device-local layout (`inventory.sidebar.layout`), never account preferences. Sidebar identity/profile stay pinned while destinations scroll; single-destination groups are direct links. Native More preserves the same authorized destinations. Preferences group Basic (theme/density/control size), Advanced styling/performance, and regional/list behavior; display device constraints without overwriting saved choices. Setup progress uses only server checklist flags.

- **DS-074** [review] POS keeps the characterized shared transaction model. Held carts use existing accessible collapsibles without unmounting drafts; narrow web layouts expose a cart jump and native retains its cart dock. Desktop cart constraints and the two-column breakpoint must agree (1100px); tablet carts remain in normal flow. Receipt display/print preserve exact receiptText output; physical black/white print styles are intentional exceptions to screen tokens and never confirm printer delivery.

- **DS-075** [review] Inventory product detail uses labelled metadata and compact status groups; price history and movement history reuse existing tables (native RecordTable). Movement details open from the loaded record in FormSheet/SidePanel, retain all exact deltas/reasons/source references and identify actor IDs as references, never invented names. Existing product setup saves, archive state, stock commands and permission guards remain authoritative.

- **DS-076** [review] Purchasing keeps supplier/order creation beside its collection and supplier editing beside the selected supplier. Selected order and invoice details use existing drawers/native panels; exact line, receipt, return and settlement evidence uses tables with explicit units and reference labels. Receiving, returns and cash settlement remain separate guarded commands; presentation never completes or pays an order.

- **DS-077** [review] Warehouse scanning separates product, location and count-review context without posting on scan. Count evidence uses exact server quantities, explicit hidden/not-counted values and a recount warning for stale lines; never infer expected stock during blind capture. Storage metadata uses RecordDetails and warehouse totals use Table/RecordTable with explicit empty states. Retain scoped movement/reservation commands and label root versus direct-location balances.

- **DS-078** [review] Transfer lists keep draft creation with collection controls; detail drawers/native panels distinguish route metadata, lines, receipts and event history. Show selected-unit quantities separately from approved/settled base units and good/damaged/shortage receipts. Use loaded authorized warehouse names, label unresolved identifiers as references and never infer receipt time or actor names. Existing state-specific confirmation forms own all transitions.

- **DS-079** [review] Cash shifts use a compact reconciliation table and loaded-record detail drawer/native panel; expected/counted/discrepancy stay exact currency minor units, with uncounted values explicit. Shift commands remain scoped to the selected record. Sales retain exact receiptText/print adapters; separate recorded return/refund evidence from authorized correction commands and never infer refund success or printer delivery.

- **DS-080** [review] Customer drawers separate profile and credit policy from recorded receivables, cash payments, credits, refunds and customer prices. Use existing details and table primitives with exact units, business-timezone timestamps, explicit missing-history states and secondary references. Editing, archival, credit and payment forms retain their scoped permissions and original commands; retention remains in Business settings.

- **DS-081** [review] Payables compares server balances in separate currency rows and exact minor units; invoice drawers separate supplier context, balances, uncredited returns and recorded settlement history. Use readable event labels and business-timezone dates, keeping missing references explicit. Warehouse/supplier filters and guarded cash/credit commands retain their existing query, scope and retry identities.

- **DS-082** [review] Accounting separates all-date, per-currency trial balances from paged periods, journals and unposted sources. Journal drawers retain exact debit/credit lines, posting dates and source/reversal references; show recorded timestamps in business timezone without changing UTC posting/period rules. Pending counts never imply reconciliation. Original permission, confirmation and idempotent command paths remain authoritative.

- **DS-083** [review] Reports present the loaded response's category, UTC date range, as-of timestamp, exact units and current-page scope together. Keep current inventory/outstanding balances distinct from period flows; preserve server notes and separate currencies. Exports contain loaded rows with unchanged columns, never a silently expanded dataset. Browser print uses legible paper tables and context without navigation, filters or duplicate metric cards; native retains its export adapter. Do not fabricate charts from unrelated measures or change legacy UTC aggregation during visual work.

- **DS-084** [review] Business trading presents relationship references, shared order terms and on-demand event history separately. Preserve exact agreed quantities/units/prices; identify unknown counterparties by business reference, never invent names. History timestamps use the business timezone; coordination states do not post stock or money. Existing bilateral consent, versioned commands and retry identities remain authoritative; filters cannot exceed the API's offset-only support.

- **DS-085** [review] Integrations distinguish server-reported Built-in only, Not configured and Enabled states; none is a live connection test. Retain operator-owned configuration guidance and permission-filtered navigation labels. Show navigation-only assistant controls solely for explicitly enabled AI; never add credential inputs, activation shortcuts or inferred provider readiness during presentation work.

# Development and verification

## Setup and commands

- **DEV-001** [review] Use Node 24.x and npm 11.x (pinned packageManager in root package.json), one root lockfile and npm workspaces. Run `npm ci`, `npm run setup`, `npm run doctor`, then `npm run dev` for web/API plus repository-local PostgreSQL. Setup preserves existing environment files; use the workspace `.env.example` files, never commit credentials. PostgreSQL binaries must be on PATH or under `PG_BIN`.
- **DEV-002** [review] Default local ports: web 5173, desktop 5174, API 3100, Metro 8081, isolated PostgreSQL 5433. Do not kill unrelated processes to free ports. `npm run db:local -- stop` preserves repository-local data. Verify API readiness before exercising database workflows.
- **DEV-003** [review] Task: Independent dev; Command: `npm run dev:web`, `dev:api`, `dev:mobile`, `dev:desktop`
- **DEV-004** [review] Task: Native launch; Command: `npm run android`, `npm run ios`; requires SDK/emulator or hardware
- **DEV-005** [review] Task: Code quality; Command: `npm run format:check`, `check:foundation`, `check:parity`, `lint`, `typecheck`
- **DEV-006** [review] Task: Tests; Command: `npm test`; `npm run test:integration` against isolated test PostgreSQL
- **DEV-007** [review] Task: Browser; Command: `npm run test:web:browser`; shell scenarios use their existing Playwright config
- **DEV-008** [review] Task: Build; Command: `npm run build` (API/web); `build:mobile` (JS export); `build:desktop` (host native tools)
- **DEV-009** [review] Task: Audit inventory; Command: `npm run audit:ui` writes source/route evidence under artifacts, not docs
- **DEV-010** [review] Task: Demo; Command: Existing `dev:mock:web/mobile/desktop` and `db:seed:dev/showcase/transactions`; never production
- **DEV-011** [review] Task: Deployment; Command: `npm run package:api`; `package:desktop:remote` or `package:desktop:local`
- **DEV-012** [review] Task: Backup; Command: `npm run db:backup -- --help`; verify restore into an isolated destination before release
- **DEV-013** [review] Web/desktop need a valid `VITE_API_BASE_URL`; native uses its existing `EXPO_PUBLIC_*` origin. Client values are embedded/public. Production HTTPS, API CORS and exact desktop CSP media origins must agree. `DESKTOP_IMAGE_ORIGINS` is an explicit HTTPS allowlist, not `https:*`. Android emulator host access normally uses 10.0.2.2; real devices need a reachable permitted API. Never weaken production TLS for local development.
- **DEV-014** [review] Migrations are versioned files under `apps/api/migrations`, executed explicitly using the API workspace's `db:migrate`; never edit applied migrations or auto-migrate at app startup. Inspect workspace scripts for exact options. API artifacts deploy independently: inject production config/secrets, migrate, start. Desktop local-network edition requires a separately deployed server/database; it is not an embedded multi-device database.

## Workflow and reusable commands

- **DEV-015** [review] Read AGENTS, then only the relevant guide. Inspect actual implementations, routes, models, schemas and consumers before editing.
- **DEV-016** [review] Record impact: source/permissions → transaction → contracts/events → cache/outbox → web/native/desktop adapters → tests. Mark absent layers and unknowns.
- **DEV-017** [review] Extend existing components and models; keep scope and business behavior explicit. Target cohesive 100–150-line sources; review >200 and record justified exceptions in `scripts/source-size-exceptions.json`.
- **DEV-018** [review] Validate success/failure, permissions, isolation, retries, rollback and relevant preference/device states. Review final diff; preserve unrelated changes and do not commit.
- **DEV-019** [review] Report exact commands/results, actual screen/role/viewport evidence, unrun checks, blockers and follow-up. Build success is not runtime qualification.
- **DEV-020** [review] `/milestone`: implement only named items after confirming their current scope; old milestone specs are historical inputs, not blanket authority. If only a number is given and its detailed spec is unavailable, ask for that scope before implementing. `/milestone-1-decisions`: review existing accepted decisions in architecture/security guides; do not execute business features from a decision review. `/parity-check`: inspect registries, route visibility, native equivalents, adapters and failure/offline states; run check:parity and record tested versus code-only coverage. `/visual-qa`: inspect every applicable route/role with existing mock fixtures; test responsive/theme/preference/error/empty/offline states, fix in scope, record screenshots and results under `artifacts/qa`. Never fabricate production data or device results.

## Release qualification

- **DEV-021** [review] Record artifact version/hash, OS/browser/device, role/scenario and result; checklist remains open until evidence exists for that artifact.
- **DEV-022** [review] Gate: Build/install; Web: Production Vite deploy, HTTPS/CSP/SW; Windows: Windows-host Tauri installer, signing/WebView2, clean install/upgrade; macOS: Target-architecture Tauri app/DMG, signing, notarization, Gatekeeper
- **DEV-023** [review] Gate: Runtime; Web: Real API login/navigation/POS/receipt/stock/roles; Windows: Installed app, narrow/fullscreen, lock/restart; macOS: Installed WKWebView app, resize/lock/restart
- **DEV-024** [review] Gate: Offline vault; Web: IndexedDB quota/eviction, offline reload, grant expiry and sync; Windows: SQLite WAL, concurrent claims/crash/disk pressure/upgrade; macOS: SQLite WAL, interruption/permissions/sleep/upgrade
- **DEV-025** [review] Gate: Printing; Web: Actual supported browser/printer, cancel/reprint; Windows: Actual scanner/printer/driver and cancelled print; macOS: Actual scanner/printer, native dialog and cancellation
- **DEV-026** [review] Gate: Deep links; Web: Configured HTTPS invite/recovery, invalid/expired/replay; Windows: Installed inventory: registration, cold/warm/single-instance; macOS: Launch Services inventory:, cold/warm/single-instance
- **DEV-027** [review] Gate: Remote images; Web: Trusted allowlist/error placeholder, no private leakage; Windows: Emitted CSP, actual WebView2 hosts/TLS denial; macOS: Emitted CSP, actual WKWebView hosts/TLS denial
- **DEV-028** [review] Gate: Updates; Web: Old/new shell compatibility, no forced checkout reload; Windows: Signed replacement/update preserves vault/outbox; macOS: Signed/notarized replacement preserves vault/outbox
- **DEV-029** [review] Gate: Real hardware; Web: Offline/reload, scanner/printer, browser accessibility; Windows: Physical supported Windows host and peripherals; macOS: Physical Mac for every advertised architecture/peripheral
- **DEV-030** [review] Android/iOS are parity targets, not launch gates: JS export is insufficient. Qualify signed native install, SQLite/SecureStore, safe areas/keyboard, TalkBack/VoiceOver, links, camera/printing, process death and sync on emulator plus relevant physical hardware. Missing tools/devices must be reported, not bypassed.
- **DEV-031** [review] CI plan (not installed): Linux quality + isolated PostgreSQL integration + web build/browser artifact; Windows runner with Rust/MSVC/WebView2 installer build; macOS runner with Xcode/Rust app/DMG build. Publish checksummed artifacts/logs. Keep signing/notarization secrets on protected release jobs; do not expose to untrusted PRs. Physical-device/peripheral gates remain manual.

## Documentation history

- **DEV-032** [review] There are exactly four active guides in this folder; AGENTS is the short root entry point and README is startup only. Keep new decisions/invariants in the owning guide; put component prop detail in typed source and examples in the showcase. Do not add stage diaries or duplicate instructions here.
- **DEV-033** [review] The consolidation preserved every original docs file, including untracked specifications/prompts and QA evidence, in `artifacts/documentation-consolidation/original-docs.tar.gz`; `manifest.json` contains paths, byte counts and SHA-256 hashes verified against the archive. Archive paths start with `docs/`. Root instructions/README also have a separate snapshot. This is a local ignored archive, not a committed or remote backup: retain it when transferring this work and recover a historical spec from it when explicitly needed. It is historical evidence, not automatically active instructions.
- **DEV-034** [review] Generated screenshots/data now live under `artifacts/qa`; executable parity exceptions live in `scripts/parity-exceptions.json`. Tests/tools write outside docs. Workflow wrappers point here instead of deleted prompt paths. Source scan evidence is `artifacts/ui-audit/source-inventory.json`; it distinguishes limited static checks from visual review.

## Redesign verification and performance

- **DEV-035** [review] Redesign matrices and run evidence belong in `.ai/reports/redesign/`, never canonical guides. Baseline snapshots are evidence, not instructions. Use `npm run redesign:inventory` to regenerate route/component evidence and `npm run check:redesign` to reject missing/stale route rows and invalid guides. Review source consumers rather than treating import closure as proof of runtime reachability.
- **DEV-036** [review] Use the named phase branch; do not commit. Tag the Phase 1 baseline with an annotation identifying the current HEAD and uncommitted evidence; never imply a Git tag includes working-tree changes. A later implementation/release tag requires an authorized reviewed commit.
- **DEV-037** [review] Use mock/scenario data on a loopback server for screenshot baselines, with fixed date, locale, timezone and documented image/network behavior. Capture every web destination at desktop/mobile widths and both themes; document native-only and inaccessible states. Browser viewports are not native or installed Tauri qualification.
- **DEV-038** [review] For each phase, report raw/gzip production chunk and CSS bytes plus measured list readiness and search latency using the same fixture, viewport and machine. Treat growth or latency regression above 10% as a review trigger, not proof of failure; explain intentional tradeoffs before acceptance. No new heavy dependency, unbounded list fetch or changed search debounce without approval. Distinguish development mock timings from production/user performance.
- **DEV-039** [review] Retain all baseline failures with exact commands. Fix only task-related tooling in Phase 1; do not weaken assertions or change application behavior to obtain green results. Integration requires an isolated TEST_DATABASE_URL; desktop/mobile require host tools and runtime evidence.

- **DEV-040** [enforced: npm run check:docs] Keep exactly four canonical guides, each at most 200 lines, with unique rule IDs, review/enforcement tags and valid local links and anchors.

- **DEV-041** [enforced: npm run audit:ui] Run the design regression guard through audit:ui/validate. Review baseline entries individually; do not regenerate it to hide new violations. Keep screenshots and computed-style probes separate from native/device qualification.

- **DEV-042** [enforced: npm run check:redesign-budget] After a production web build, compare all JS/CSS chunk bytes against Phase 1; >10% growth fails the review guard. Run `scripts/redesign-performance.mjs` separately on a quiet mock server; compare cold/warm readiness and search with Phase 1, recording sample variance rather than asserting production INP.
- **DEV-043** [review] Retained POS screens preserve drafts and recovery; idle hidden checkout may stop invalidation polling, but nonempty/held/pending/uncertain carts retain it. Resume reads authoritative revisions. Do not unmount transactions, pause security/session checks or add virtualization without measured evidence.
